note: Numbers are spelled out on purpose: the model reads digits inconsistently, and the verifier compares what it actually said against this script word for word.

direction._: calm, warm, unhurried; one person speaking to one person in a quiet room
direction.enter: welcoming and low, almost confiding; nothing is being sold
direction.morning: brisk and practical, a working voice; slight forward pressure, never alarmed
direction.freeze: quiet and open, straight after a noise stops; a real question, not a challenge
direction.reflection: gentle and curious; the listener is not being assessed
direction.transition: even and kind; setting something down before picking something up
direction.context: plain and factual, an assistant reading a list
direction.second: the same practical voice as the morning, with less pressure
direction.mirror: steady and non-judgemental; whichever of these is true, it is not a verdict
direction.end: quiet close, then one step forward
direction.name: one word, said plainly, as if reading a name off a list; a small pause at the end
direction.you: warm and neutral, handing something back rather than announcing it
direction.ready: unhurried, an invitation with no pressure in it at all
direction.pulseback: soft and generous, letting someone else be right

en.enter-4: Choose what makes sense to you.
en.morning: Your morning is already moving. You have thirty seconds. Choose the two things you would deal with first.
en.transition-1: You made a choice with the context you had.
en.transition-2: Now let us add what you could not see.
en.context: The same information, with what sat underneath it.
en.second: Same morning. More context. You have thirty seconds. Choose two again.
en.mirror: Your experience did not change. The information available to you did.
en.end: Pulse One complete. Signal. But noticing something does not make it true.
en.ready: Take your time. Continue when you are ready.
en.mirror-both: More context changed what deserved your attention.
en.mirror-one: Some instincts held. One changed with context.
en.mirror-none: More context reinforced your first judgment.
en.context-2: Each one now shows who owns it, what it needs, and what happens if it waits.
en.end-next: Next Pulse. Truth. What do you trust?
en.pulseback: Someone else may have chosen differently. And they may have had a good reason.

id.enter-4: Pilih yang paling masuk akal bagimu.
id.morning: Pagimu sudah jalan duluan. Kamu punya tiga puluh detik. Pilih dua yang mau kamu tangani duluan.
id.transition-1: Kamu memilih dengan konteks yang kamu punya waktu itu.
id.transition-2: Sekarang, kita tambahkan yang tadi belum kelihatan.
id.context: Informasi yang sama, plus apa yang ada di baliknya.
id.second: Pagi yang sama. Konteksnya lebih lengkap. Kamu punya tiga puluh detik. Pilih dua lagi.
id.mirror: Yang berubah bukan pengalamanmu. Tapi informasi yang kamu punya.
id.end: Pulse Satu selesai. Signal. Tapi memperhatikan sesuatu tidak otomatis bikin hal itu benar.
id.ready: Santai saja. Lanjut kalau sudah siap.
id.mirror-both: Setelah konteksnya lebih lengkap, yang menurutmu perlu diperhatikan jadi berubah.
id.mirror-one: Sebagian pilihanmu bertahan. Satu berubah setelah konteksnya lebih lengkap.
id.mirror-none: Konteks tambahan justru menguatkan pilihan awalmu.
id.context-2: Sekarang setiap informasi menunjukkan siapa pemiliknya, apa yang dibutuhkan, dan apa akibatnya jika ditunda.
id.end-next: Pulse berikutnya. Truth. Apa yang kamu percaya?
id.pulseback: Orang lain mungkin memilih yang berbeda. Dan alasannya bisa jadi masuk akal juga.
id.you-context: Setelah ada konteks tambahan, kamu memilih.
